_meta.indication: VIIBRYD is indicated for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD); efficacy established in two 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in adult patients with MDD.

pivotal_trials.design: U.S., randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, 8-week study; patients titrated to target dose by Day 15
pivotal_trials.population: Adult (18-70 years) outpatients meeting DSM-IV-TR criteria for major depressive disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 8 in the MADRS total score
pivotal_trials.result: MADRS LS mean difference from placebo -2.5 (95% CI -4.4, -0.6); P-value 0.009

nct_ctgov.title: Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Study of Vilazodone's Efficacy, Safety, and Biomarkers of Response in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)

pivotal_trials.design: U.S., randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, 8-week study; patients randomized 1:1 to placebo or vilazodone, titrated to target dose by Day 15
pivotal_trials.population: Adult (18-70 years) outpatients meeting DSM-IV-TR criteria for major depressive disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 8 in the MADRS total score
pivotal_trials.result: MADRS LS mean difference from placebo -3.2 (95% CI -5.1, -1.2); P-value 0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Effectiveness Study of Vilazodone to Treat Depression and to Discover Genetic Markers Associated With Response

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and at least twice the rate of placebo): diarrhea (28% vs 9%), nausea (23% vs 5%), vomiting (5% vs 1%), and insomnia (6% vs 2%).
target_moa: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT1A receptor partial agonist; antidepressant effect thought related to enhancement of serotonergic activity in the CNS through selective inhibition of serotonin reuptake, with high-affinity serotonin reuptake binding (Ki=0.1 nM).

boxed_warning.content: Suicidality and Antidepressant Drugs: antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies of MDD and other psychiatric disorders.

rems.type: REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication.

description.text: Added a new dosing regimen (fixed 20 mg and 40 mg doses) to the Dosage and Administration section for adults with MDD

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides revisions to include a new dosing regimen under the dosing and administration section of the Viibryd label.

description.text: Added safety information for pediatric patients ages 7 to 17 years with Major Depressive Disorder

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of safety information in pediatric patients ages 7 years to 17 years of age with Major Depressive Disorder.

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b) for the treatment of major depressive disorder, approved on a first review cycle; not referred to an advisory committee because the drug is not first in its class, with a required Medication Guide REMS and PREA pediatric study requirements.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated March 22, 2010, received March 22, 2010, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Viibryd (vilazodone hydrochloride) 10 mg, 20 mg, and 40 mg tablets.

Your application for vilazodone was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class, and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication.
The REMS consists of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

requirement.text: 1723-1: Deferred pediatric study under PREA in MDD patients aged 7 to 17 to obtain pharmacokinetic, safety, and tolerability data pertinent to dosing of vilazodone.

citations.quote: 1723-1	Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of major depressive disorder in pediatric patients aged 7 to 17. Conduct a study to obtain pharmacokinetic, safety, and tolerability data and provide information pertinent to dosing of vilazodone in the relevant pediatric population.	Final Protocol Submission Date: January 31, 2012

requirement.text: 1723-2: Deferred pediatric efficacy/safety study under PREA in MDD patients aged 7 to 17; placebo-controlled and active-controlled (fluoxetine), fixed-dose study.

citations.quote: 1723-2	Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of major depressive disorder in pediatric patients aged 7 to 17. Conduct a study to obtain data on the efficacy and safety of vilazodone in the relevant pediatric population. This must be a placebo-controlled and active-controlled (fluoxetine) study. This study must be a fixed-dose study.

requirement.text: 1723-3: Second deferred pediatric efficacy/safety study under PREA in MDD patients aged 7 to 17; placebo-controlled and active-controlled (fluoxetine) study.

citations.quote: 1723-3	Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of major depressive disorder in pediatric patients aged 7 to 17. Conduct a second study to obtain data on the efficacy and safety of vilazodone in the relevant pediatric population. This must be a placebo-controlled and active-controlled (fluoxetine) study. This study may be a fixed-dose study.

requirement.text: 1723-4: Conduct a juvenile rat study to assess the safety of vilazodone in children less than 13 years of age, including neurological/behavioral and reproductive development.

citations.quote: 1723-4	To support the use of vilazodone in children less than 13 years of age, you must conduct a study to assess the safety of vilazodone in juvenile rats. This study must include evaluation of neurological/behavioral development and reproductive development. You should submit the protocol for our comments prior to initiating the study.	Final Protocol Submission Date: January 30, 2012

requirement.text: 1723-5: Assess reproductive toxicity of metabolite M17 by conducting an embryo-fetal study in rats or rabbits with M17 administered to produce systemic exposure ≥ the exposure in humans at the MRHD.

citations.quote: 1723-5 Assess the reproductive toxicity of metabolite M17 by conducting an embryo-fetal study in either rats or rabbits in which M17 is administered by a route that will produce systemic exposure equal to or greater than the exposure in humans at the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD).

requirement.text: 1723-6: Assess reproductive toxicity of metabolite M17 by demonstrating that the original rabbit study adequately assessed M17 embryo-fetal toxicity.

citations.quote: 1723-6 Assess the reproductive toxicity of metabolite M17 by demonstrating that the original rabbit study was adequate to assess the embryo-fetal toxicity of M17. This will require data demonstrating that the systemic exposure to M17 in rabbits in that study was equal to or greater than that in humans at the MRHD.

requirement.text: 1723-7: A placebo-controlled, randomized-withdrawal controlled trial to evaluate longer-term (maintenance) efficacy of vilazodone in adults with MDD.

citations.quote: 1723-7 A controlled trial to evaluate the longer-term (i.e., maintenance) efficacy of vilazodone in the treatment of adults with major depressive disorder. This trial must be placebo-controlled, utilize a randomized withdrawal design, and include an adequate period of stabilization with open-label treatment of vilazodone prior to double-blind randomization.

requirement.text: 1723-8: Further characterize efficacy and safety of vilazodone in adults with MDD using fixed doses (20 mg and 40 mg), an active control, and placebo in an adequate and well-controlled trial.

citations.quote: 1723-8 It is not apparent from the trials you have conducted in major depressive disorder that the lowest effective dose of vilazodone has been identified, because only one dose (40 mg/day) was studied.

Thus, we request that you further characterize the efficacy and safety of vilazodone in the treatment of adults with MDD using fixed doses of vilazodone (20 mg and 40 mg), an active control (for assay sensitivity), and placebo in an adequate and well controlled trial.

requirement.text: 1723-9: Conduct a drug-drug interaction trial of vilazodone using a CYP3A4 inducer (carbamazepine) in healthy subjects.

citations.quote: 1723-9 Vilazodone is metabolized primarily by CYP3A4. You have not submitted information on the potential effect of CYP3A4 induction on vilazodone exposure. We request that you conduct a drug-drug interaction trial of vilazodone using a CYP3A4 inducer (carbamazepine) in healthy subjects.

requirement.text: 1723-10: Conduct a Phase 1 trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of vilazodone in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

citations.quote: 1723-10 Vilazodone is extensively metabolized; however, the pharmacokinetics of vilazodone in patients with severe hepatic impairment has not been assessed. We request that you conduct a Phase 1 trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of vilazodone in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

requirement.text: 1723-11: Conduct an in vitro study to evaluate whether vilazodone is a substrate or inhibitor of PgP.

citations.quote: 1723-11 Information on the effect of PgP on the pharmacokinetics of vilazodone and the effect of vilazodone on PgP was not submitted. We request that you conduct an in vitro study to evaluate whether vilazodone is a substrate or inhibitor of PgP.
